At the same time, the growth will be accompanied by an increase in energy production and domestic demand. The economy is expected to grow in 2024 against the backdrop of the end of the negative impact of shocks and a significant increase in production, taking into account the implementation of large oil and gas projects. THIRD. FOREIGN ECONOMIC CONDITION. Inflation in the world and in trade partner countries is accelerating. Inflation in the eurozone reached a record 8.1% in May this year. In April, inflation in Russia accelerated to 17.8%, in China - to 2.1%. The unfao food price index was close to a record low of 157.4 points in May this year, despite a slight decline for two consecutive months. In May, prices for vegetable oil, dairy products and sugar decreased. At the same time, small indices of grain and meat prices increased. We expect the peak of external inflation to coincide with the third quarter of this year, and then Inflation processes in sequence until 2024 will be reduced. Given our prerequisites and expectations of a slowdown in global demand, pressure on the external prices of feed commodities will begin to weaken next year. *** Taking into account the balance of factors, the National Bank decided to keep the base rate at 14%. Inflation risks are largely due to global inflation and uncertainty within the geopolitical situation in the world and imports of external inflation. Possible internal factors in the inflation rate are largely due to the observability of easy fiscal policies, higher inflation expectations, and the possibility of accelerated inflation of paid services after the end of the moratorium on rising prices for regulated services. Taking into account these factors and the balance of inflation risks, maintaining the current level of the base rate in the absence of new shocks will have an impact on restraining price growth in the medium term we believe. The National Bank will monitor the situation in the global market, the development of geopolitical crisis and the implementation of proinflationary risks. Further decisions on the base rate are made in connection with the fact that the real inflation dynamics corresponds to the forecast trajectory, as well as the balance of risks in the medium-sized economy. We remind that the next decision on the base rate will be announced on July 25, 2022 at 15:00 pm Nur-Sultan city time. *** Dear journalists! *** In summary, I would like to informs that we have published a review report (green paper) on digital assets and non-centralized finance on June 6. As a result of the announcement, we plan to hold a series of discussions with market participants, government agencies and the expert community in order to develop a comprehensive state approach to the development and regulation of digital assets and decentralized finance. The development of the digital assets and decentralized finance (DeFi) industry is one of the most important factors in the attention of regulators. The National Bank will not limit the innovative potential of digital assets and DeFi, but will not limit the consumers of financial services and macro-financial stability balance sheet adjustment policy that provides protection provides for the possibility of development. Thank you for your attention!

Title: Statement on the base rate of the National Bank of The Republic of Kazakhstan By the Chairman of the National Bank Of Kazakhstan Pirmatov G.O. on September 5, 2022 Nur-Sultan
text: Statement on the base rate of the National Bank of The Republic of Kazakhstan By the Chairman of the National Bank Of Kazakhstan Pirmatov G.O. on September 5, 2022 Nur-Sultan Dear representatives of the mass media! The National Bank continues to announce decisions on the base rate within the framework of the press briefing. Today We are ready to answer your questions after the briefing, talking about the factors of the decision i announced. The Monetary Policy Committee of the National Bank decided to keep the base rate at the level of 14.5% since September 6, 2022. The decision was made on the basis of the results of the next forecast round. We have changed our forecasts for the further development of the macroeconomic situation, renewing our expectations for inflation and real GDP growth until the end of this year and in the medium term. Let me begin to explain the factors of the decision on the base rate. *** THE FIRST. INFLATION DYNAMICS. Despite the decline in the monthly inflation dynamics from the peak in March of this year (3.7%), it exceeds the average annual values (in August of the last 5 years - 0.2%) and still remains at the level of 1.4% in August. In annual terms, inflation reached 16.1%. The increase in food prices in annual terms reached 20.8%, and continues to make the largest contribution. Non-food inflation also increased to 15.5% due to the rising cost of imported goods. In particular, this applies to household goods, as well as stationery, as part of the growth of demand. Inflation of paid services reached 10.1%. The highest increase in prices for the rental of furnished housing is observed. In connection with the end of the moratorium on increasing tariffs until July 1, 2022, tariffs for the services of monopoly enterprises were changed in all regions. Thus, their monthly growth was 1.3% (1.2% year-on-year). Inflation expectations are still high. In August of this year, the median annual inflation expectation was 16.5%. According to the results of the current year, in accordance with the updated forecasts, we expect inflation at 16-18%. This is higher than the previous forecast of the National Bank. The forecast revision was due to higher-than-expected real inflation and a strong fiscal boost. In the framework of high external inflation, weakening of the tenge and the restructuring of the logistics and production supply chain significant inflationary pressure will remain. High and volatile inflationary expectations will be an additional factor in price growth. In 2023, inflation will slow to 7.5-9.5%. The decline in the FAO grain index, the high base of inflation in 2022, and the faster-than-expected slowdown in Inflation in Russia will have a negative impact on inflation. Despite these positive preconditions, a stronger fiscal stimulus has not allowed us to revise our 2023 forecast downwards. In 2024, in the absence of new external and internal shocks, inflation will be near targeted. According to our estimates, it will be formed at the level of 5.5-7.5%. Pro-cyclical fiscal policy remains the main inflation factor in the medium term. THE SECOND. THE STATE OF THE DOMESTIC ECONOMY. Growth of gross domestic product for 7 months of this year amounted to 3.3%. Due to the repair works in Kashagan and the irrevocations in the production processes of the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, the slowdown in economic growth is caused by the reduction of oil production in the country. Manufacturing, trade, construction and transport industries contributed positively to the growth of the economy. Total internal the main driver of the growth of production is the construction sector is staying. In the context of the slowdown in economic activity, uncertainty about the work of the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, as well as planned repairs at the remaining two large deposits, economic growth in 2022 was revised downwards. According to the results of 2022, gdp growth will be 2.5-3.5%. The prevailing high price situation and the growth rate of oil production by the end of the year all domestic demand as part of the recovery components and real exports make a positive contribution continues. Further, we expect acceleration of economic growth in 2023-2024 against the background of increased exports as a result of the increase in oil production. In the context of the growth of public spending, the positive dynamics of consumer demand will be an additional incentive. At the same time, the increase in fiscal stimulus will partially equalize GDP growth. As a result, gdp growth in 2023 is expected at the level of 4-5%. In 2024, the dynamics of economic growth will remain at the same rate as part of the reduction of negative shocks and a significant increase in production, taking into account the implementation of large oil and gas projects. The positive pace of lending by banks continues to support the economy. Second-tier loan portfolio of banks January-July of this year during the months of 20.4 trillion tenge increased by 10.1%, including loans to enterprises - to 8.0 trillion tenge. In general, we see the positive growth of lending after the normalization of the banking system, the increase in its stability, which has contributed to an increase in the capitalization of banks and a gradual reduction in the share of non-performing loans in the portfolio of second-tier banks from 9.3% in 2017 to 3.8% by the end of July 2022 (at the end of 2021 - 3.3%). At the same time, in the current context of growing uncertainty and the adjustment of the economy to new external conditions, of course, long-term projects are being revised, which will also affect lending. The demand for credit products plays an important role in the prospects for the development of the macroeconomic situation, as well as the expectations of borrowers of their ability to repay debt at present or in the future. The National Bank attaches great importance to creating conditions for long-term and sound economic growth, including the availability of sources of financing of the economy. THIRD. EXTERNAL ECONOMIC CONDITION. In July and August of this year, the FAO food price index decreased significantly by 9% and 1.9%, respectively. This is mainly vegetable oil as a result of the decline in the price of cereals he's got it. The decline in grain prices was mainly due to the agreement reached between Ukraine and the Russian Federation on the opening of ukraine's main Black Sea ports and the start of harvesting in the northern hemisphere. All this has contributed to the increase in supply. Inflation in the world is still at an all-time high, requiring a strict monetary policy from central banks. In the world commodity markets, relatively high oil prices are expected to remain. According to the forecasts of international organizations, the average price of Brent crude oil in 2022 will be 105 dollars per barrel, and in 2023 it will be 90 dollars per barrel. *** Taking into account the factors, the National Bank decided to keep the base rate at 14.5%. The current level of the base rate ensures the stability of the financial market and supports the accumulation activity of economic entities. The current inflation depends on the adaptation of domestic prices to external price changes. In addition, since the beginning of the year, significant increases in the base rate have been introduced into the economy. the effect has not yet been fully observed and is relevant in the future requires an evaluation. Measures taken by the National Bank: 1) In general, it allowed to increase the volume of deposits in tenge, reduce the dollarization of deposits and protect assets in tenge. Since June, there has been an increase in deposits in tenge. The total volume of deposits reached the historical highest level of 28.1 trillion tenge. The dollarization of deposits decreased from the highest level of 38.4% in February to 35.4% at the end of July of this year, and the increase in deposits (more than 50 million tenge) of the population, with the exception of large deposits, reached a record low mark of 15%. 2) Allowed to continue the growth of lending. In July of this year, loans to the economy were increased by 27.1% to 20.4 trillion tenge due to the annual crediting of the population and business in tenge, starting from the beginning of this year - increased by 10.1%. On August 27, the National Bank began to publish the expanded statistics on lending to the economy. Taking into account other financial institutions, the total amount of lending to the economy is 24.2 trillion tenge. tenge was created. 3) allowed to achieve a balance in the currency market. Since April this year, the National Bank has not carried out interventions to sell foreign currency, and in August it did not sell foreign currency to ensure transfers from the National Fund to the republican budget. Transfers to the National Fund at the expense of revenues in tenge provided. Further decisions on the base rate will be taken in accordance with the projected trajectory of inflation, as well as the balance of risks in the middle and agro-industrial environment. I remind that the next decision on the base rate will be announced on October 24, 2022 at 14:00 pm Nur-Sultan city time. *** Dear journalists! Macroeconomic opinions among the national banking expert community in August 2022 i would like to informs you that it has published its first results. We will always try to conduct dialogue with different audiences, developing our communication policy in detail. The purpose of these comments is to improve the dialogue of the National Bank with the professional community, thereby reducing the information gap between the market and the regulator. At the same time, I would like to note that we do not intend to create new markets. We would like to know different opinions on the development of the situation in domestic and global markets. As part of my macroeconomic opinions, we also plan to discuss our forecasts. For this purpose, after the publication of the Monetary Policy Report, we plan to hold meetings with my participants, where we will share our plans and forecasts for the future. Thank you for your attention!

Title: Statement of the Chairman of the National Bank of Kazakhstan Pirmatov G.O. on the base rate of the National Bank (October 26, 2022, Astana)
text: Statement of Chairman of the National Bank of Kazakhstan Pirmatov G.O. on the base rate of the National Bank on October 26, 2022, Astana Dear representatives of the mass media! Dear journalists. Good day. Welcome to the National Bank. I will tell you about the factors of the decision on the base rate. Then we are ready to answer your questions. Monetary Policy Committee of the National Bank Base rate from October 27, 2022 He decided to raise the level to 16%. The decision was made due to the significant acceleration of inflation and the fact that the price growth was significantly higher than our forecast estimates. By the end of this year, we expected inflation to be between 16 and 18%. In September, real inflation exceeded the forecast: acceleration of inflation expectations, stability of components of inflation in the framework of a positive fiscal dynamics, high external inflation, disruption of commodity supply routes, higher inflation than Russia continued imports, as well as production costs as a result of the growth. There are signs of a steady rise in inflation. In this case, its rapid growth is likely to last for a long time. All this requires decisive measures aimed at tightening monetary requirements. It is necessary to avoid a significant distortion of the actual base rate for longer than its normal value. Because this will cause inflationary processes to get out of control and reduce the possibility of stabilizing inflation in the years to come. Today's decision is in line with the conditions set out in the previous decision and the forecasts of the analytical community in my ongoing macroeconomic comments. It follows the principle of pre-reaction of monetary policy and adjusts the rate figure to prevent inflationary expectations from spreading further. I will pay attention to the factors of the decision. *** THE FIRST. CURRENT AND EXPECTED INFLATION DYNAMICS. Inflation in annual terms reached 17.7%. The increase in food prices, which accelerated to 22.2%, is the largest contributor to inflation. Food inflation in the structure of eggs, vegetable oils, poultry meat, bakery there is a maximum increase in prices for products, cereals and dairy products. The seasonal decline in prices for fruit and vegetable products has had a certain disinflationary effect. In September 2022, inflation of non-food products accelerated to 17.0%. The cost of furniture, washing and cleaning equipment, household goods, coal, fuel and shoes has also increased significantly. In September 2022, the annual rate of increase in the price of paid services reached 12.3%. The main contributor to inflation was the increase in the cost of certain types of housing rental, education, housing and communal services. In September, the base inflation reached 19.7% (in August - 17.8%) and showed a steady increase in annual inflation. This confirms the high rate of increase in prices for goods and services. The rapid growth of consumer prices is observed in all indicators. For example, inflation has been rising steadily in recent months, excluding seasonal factors. Its annual rate increased to 23.2% in August after slowing to 17.7% in July, accelerating to 26.8% in September. Inflationary expectations of the population are growing. This year In September of this year, the median assessment of inflation, expected for the next year, was 16.9%. Respondents attribute this to changes in food and fuel prices, external events, as well as changes in the exchange rate. This is due to the migration shock, which, despite its temporary nature, has a significant impact on inflation expectations. According to the results of my macroeconomic comments among representatives of the expert community, we noticed a significant increase in forecasts for future inflation: the inflation forecast for 2022 increased from 15.1% in August to 18.5% in August and increased to 11% by 2023, which is 2.2 percentage points more than in August. THE SECOND. FACTORS OF THE DOMESTIC ECONOMY. With high oil prices, a significant fiscal stimulus based on the active use of funds from the National Fund remains one of the main proinflationary factors in the economy. Active fiscal policy has an impact on inflation by contributing to the growth of the money supply (M3). Since the beginning of the year, the money supply has increased by 7.9% or 2.4 trillion tenge. State budget expenditures faster than inflation is growing at a faster pace. Within the framework of the growth of inflationary processes, the stable dynamics of consumer demand parameters remains. The volume of nominal retail trade turnover for the first nine months of 2022 increased by 15.7% compared to the previous year. The growth of consumer loans of individuals from demand will create additional proinflationary pressures. For 9 months, consumer credit increased by 21.4% compared to the same period last year. For 9 months of this year, the growth of gross domestic product was in line with our forecast and amounted to 2.8%. The slowdown in business activity was mainly due to weak dynamics in the mining sector. It is connected with the repair of the main deposits of the country and the accident at the Kashagan plant. Manufacturing, trade, information and communications, transport and agriculture contribute positively to gdp growth. There is no deviation of the dynamics of economic development from our forecast. Growth of gross domestic product will be provided with a positive trajectory of domestic demand and real exports in the context of prevailing price situation and recovery of oil production by the end of the year. At the same time, the risks hindering the sustainable development of Kazakhstan's economy are being created by the growing inflationary processes. THIRD. FOREIGN ECONOMIC CONDITION. The situation in the external sector remains uncertain. The world prices for food are falling. The FAO index decreased by 1.1% in September this year. The reason for this is the reduction in the price of vegetable oils. But grain prices are rising. The increase in wheat prices is due to the possibility of sending grain from The Black Sea ports of Ukraine and the weather conditions in Argentina and the United States. Consumer inflation in the world is still high. The double-digit rate of price growth is observed not only in developing economies, but also in a number of developed economies. In such cases, the leading central banks issuing reserve currencies continue to tighten monetary requirements. For us, this means an increase in the risk of increasing pressure on the exchange rate of tenge. Measures are required to ensure the attractiveness of assets in tenge by increasing the base rate. In the world oil market, there are factors in different directions affecting prices. Lower prices are caused by weak demand forecasts and rising U.S. inventories. Russia and the Middle East Problems in the supply of goods from some eastern countries, Also, the decline in the total oil production quota in OPEC countries supports the price increase. According to the forecasts of the U.S. Energy Information Administration, Brent prices will average 93 per barrel in the 4th quarter of this year and 95 per barrel in 2023. * * * Dear journalists! In accordance with its mandate, the National Bank will carefully study the current situation and make decisions on monetary policy based on the assessment of the prospects for further development. The main task for us is to maintain price stability. Now this is especially important, because high inflation, first of all, has a negative impact on difficult categories of people's social status and affects their ability to ensure a decent quality of life. It is necessary to make the most decisive decision on the monetary policy, which will hold the value of assets in tenge and preserve confidence in the national currency. We are doing everything possible to prevent the devaluation of the money of our citizens and to create opportunities for the growth of lending by the banking sector. In this regard, taking into account the above factors, the National Bank decided to raise the base rate to 16% per annum. As part of the next decision, our estimated estimates of inflation and other macroeconomic indicators will be revised. In addition, a more precise assessment of the level of the base rate required to ensure the planned fall in inflation will be carried out from 2023. If the current increase in the base rate is insufficient, the National Bank will consider the possibility of further tightening of monetary requirements. The probability of this scenario is estimated to be high. The dynamics of inflationary expectations of the subjects of the economy and the balance of risks in the external and internal environment will also be an important factor for us. Taking into account the expected inflation by the end of the year and the assessment of the requirements of the monetary credit, we have the possibility of raising the base rate. The next decision on the base rate will be announced on December 5, 2022 at 14:00 Astana time. Thank you for your attention!

Title: Statement of the Chairman of the National Bank of Kazakhstan Pirmatov G.O. on the base rate of the National Bank of Kazakhstan, December 5, 2022, Astana
text: Statement of Chairman of the National Bank of Kazakhstan Pirmatov G.O. on the base rate of the National Bank of Kazakhstan December 5, 2022 Astana Dear media representatives, dear journalists! Good day! Welcome to the National Bank! The Monetary Policy Committee of the National Bank decided to raise the base rate to 16.75% from December 6, 2022. The decision is aimed at reducing inflationary pressure and stabilizing inflation expectations. This decision was made on the basis of updated forecasts and analysis of actual data until 2025. The National Bank has approached the end of the cycle of base rate increases. The measures taken will ensure the stability of the financial market and support the accumulative activity of economic entities. The following cases prove this: 1) Since June, there has been an increase in deposits in tenge, the volume of deposits reached 30 trillion tenge. The dollarization of deposits decreased from 38.4% in February to 35.3% at the end of October. 2) The foreign exchange market is beginning to find its balance. Since April, the National Bank has not carried out interventions to sell foreign currency. We continue to adhere to a flexible rate-setting regime that avoids the accumulation of imbalances in the economy. 3) Despite the general slowdown, lending is in the positive zone. The differentiated policy will allow banks to maintain positive growth rates of lending to the economy. Thus, in October loans to the economy increased by 24.9% in annual terms to 21.5 trillion tenge due to lending to the population and business in tenge, and from the beginning of this year - by 16.1%. The decision on the base rate strengthens these processes and contributes to achieving the inflation target in the medium term. In the decisions to be made, we will focus on the fact that real inflation corresponds to the estimated estimates. *** Now I will focus on the main factors of the decision. THE FIRST. CURRENT AND EXPECTED INFLATION DYNAMICS. In November 2022, inflation in annual terms reached 19.6%. The increase in food prices, which accelerated to 24.1%, is the largest contributor to inflation. Underlying inflation remains at a high level it's coming. Speaking of inflation in monthly terms, despite the fact that in November this year it slowed to 1.4% compared to the previous two months, it remains above the perennial average and remains at a high level. Inflationary expectations of the population are close to the highest level in history. In November this year, the median inflation estimate was 18.2%. In the 4th quarter of this year, the inflation expectations of enterprises reached record highs and amounted to 17.6%. Unstable inflationary expectations due to the disruption of supply routes have stimulated consumption of short and long-term goods and led to sustained inflationary pressures. THE SECOND. FACTORS OF THE DOMESTIC ECONOMY The problems of planned and unplanned repairof the fields and the supply of Kazakhstan's exports to the world market contributed to the growth of economic activity. In the ten months of this year, gross domestic product slowed to 2.5%, which was due to lower oil production than expected. At the same time, non-oil sectors such as agriculture, communications, construction and manufacturing are growing at a high rate. Logistics delivery of consumer goods imports roads continue to be oriented towards new trade routes. As a result, the costs associated with the transition of trained trade routes, the search for new suppliers from other countries are growing. The volume of imports partially confirms the stability of the demand of enterprises and the population. Steady demand was strengthened by the growth of consumer lending, demand exceeded supply capacity. It is constrained by high inflation and a slowdown in the growth rate of real incomes of the population. Thus, according to the National Bureau of Statistics, real income growth slowed from 7.1% in the first quarter to 0.5% in the third quarter, and real wage growth slowed from 12.7% to 5.8%, respectively. Compared with consumer demand, investment activity shows a steady pace of growth. Following the results of 10 months, investments in fixed assets increased by 6.7%. Positive investment activity is observed in all key sectors of the economy. THIRD. FOREIGN ECONOMIC CONDITION. I would like to note the uncertainty of the geopolitical situation and the high level of world food prices as the main factors of the external sector. These factors are coming key factors when making decisions at the time will remain. The FAO index remained virtually unchanged in October this year. At the same time, the price of grain increased by 3% compared to the previous month. In the baseline scenario, an even decline in external food prices is expected, but their level remains high. The slowdown in the global economy continues. According to the latest forecasts of the International Monetary Fund, the growth rate of the world economy will slow to 3.2% this year. In 2023, the slowdown will continue, the growth rate will not exceed 2.7%. In many countries, inflation is accelerating, reaching the highest level in several decades. In many countries, inflation is expected to peak in the first quarter of 2023, and its return to target by the end of 2024. In this regard, we expect that in the future the external environment will be disinflationary. In the near future, the global oil market will be supported by improved demand prospects in China, the level of U.S. oil production and OPEC policy. Taking into account the current situation and forecasts of international organizations, as a prerequisite for the forecast, the price of oil in 2023 will be 90, followed by 85 per barrel in 2024. to the dollar and to 79 per barrel in 2025 will be lowered. *** We will move to the part of the forecast. Taking into account the above, the forecast in the baseline scenario was significantly revised. Until the end of 2022, inflation will be in the region of 20-21%. We expect annual inflation to peak in Q1 2023. The prolongation of the structural restructuring of trade is reflected in the non-food segment of consumer goods. As a result, high inflation expectations and disinflationary external environment have raised the inflation forecast to 11-13% by the end of 2023. Inflation is projected at 7-9% in 2024 and 4-6% in 2025. In the future, inflationary expectations in the stable environment that outperform the domestic supply capacities will be a deterrent to inflation. Further, inflation expectations will be lowered in the light of the inflationary situation and in the case of stable prices for grain crops. This will allow inflation to continue to reach target edging. Taking into account weak external demand and lower production than previously forecasted, we expect gdp growth to be 2-3% in 2022, -3-4% in 2023, and 3.54.5% in 2024-2025. In 2023, fiscal policy is expected to be in the stimulating zone, but in the framework of the application of budgetary principles, the impetus will be weakened. Nevertheless, the fiscal policy factor will continue to support government consumption and domestic demand. Further growth in demand will be a factor in supporting imports, which will limit the growth of gross domestic product. The main risks are due to uncertainty about the consequences of geopolitical tensions and its further development, the long period of structural restructuring of trade, high and volatile inflationary expectations when high feed inflation persists. The National Bank is close to the end of the base rate rise cycle. Taking into account the decision taken, the level of the base rate is estimated as high as possible. Keeping the rate at current levels for a long time will help stabilize inflation and gradually reduce it in the medium term. The likelihood of new proinflationary unexpected changes, if not, further tightening of monetary policy is low. *** Dear journalists! The National Bank will continue to take monetary policy measures aimed at reducing inflationary pressure and slowing the pace of price growth. In the medium term, monetary policy remains disinflationary, taking into account the trajectory and factors of inflation. We will continue to make further decisions on the base rate, taking into account the main objective of the National Bank to ensure price stability. Detailed information on the factors of the decision, forecasts and risks of inflation can be found in the report on monetary policy, which will be published on December 12 this year. The next decision on the base rate will be announced on January 13, 2023 at 14:00 astana time.

Title: Statement of the Chairman of the National Bank of Kazakhstan Pirmatov G.O. on the base rate of the National Bank of Kazakhstan, January 13, 2023
text: The National Bank of The Republic of Kazakhstan about base rate Statement of the Chairman of the National Bank of Kazakhstan Pirmatov G.O. January 13, 2023, Astana Dear representatives of the mass media! Dear journalists! Good day! Welcome to the National Bank! The Monetary Policy Committee of the National Bank decided to keep the base rate at 16.75% since January 16, 2023. You may know that in the previous decision we came close to ending the base rate rise cycle and estimated the probability of monetary policy tightening to be low if there were no new proinflationary shocks. Both annual and monthly inflation and economic growth dynamics are within the baseline forecast trajectory. The increase in annual inflation in December 2022 was taken into account in the previous decision. In this regard, there was no need to revise the base rate at the last meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee. However, the balance of risks is still very much on the side of high inflation. Inflation expectations, which have both sustained inflation and renewed historical maximums, are still a concern. Logistics delivery the structural changes in the roads are also negative for the economy. Our main task is to reduce the inflation trajectory and keep it that way. The main risks and factors contributing to higher inflation will require the base rate to hold at current levels over a longer period of time. * * * Now I want to talk to you about the factors that caused the decision. THE FIRST. DYNAMICS OF INFLATION AND INFLATION EXPECTATIONS. Inflation is based on the forecast trajectory. The monthly increase in consumer prices slowed and amounted to 1.2% in December last year. I should recall that the monthly inflation in September was 1.8%, in October - 1.6%, in November - 1.4%. But despite the decline in monthly inflation, it remained above the average annual values (on average in December over the past 5 years - 0.7%). Annual inflation in December 2022 was 20.3%. Prices for food products and non-food products showed the highest growth. Inflation of paid services remained unchanged, helped by a decline in the cost of renting housing and sluggish growth in regulated prices. It is also a concern that the sustained rate of inflation remains high. This indicates the preservation of the pro-inflation environment. Taking into account the seasonal factor at the end of 2022, the annual core inflation rate was 22.2%. The pace of inflation expectations prevails. Their essence has been updated to the maximum in time, which began in December when the survey was conducted. The median inflation estimate was 21.3%. According to the survey, rising food prices, external conditions and fuel prices have contributed to the rise in inflation. Higher inflation expectations could be the reason for the future slowdown and fall in inflation. THE SECOND. FACTORS OF THE DOMESTIC ECONOMY The trajectory of economic growth is formed in accordance with the basic scenario. According to preliminary estimates of the National Bureau of Statistics, gross domestic product in 2022 increased by 3.1%. The growth of business activity was mainly caused by positive dynamics in the country's commodity production. The largest growth was shown by the construction industry - by 9.4% and agriculture - by 9.1% as part of the record harvest. In the service sector, growth was observed in the trade, transport and communications sectors. In this regard, gdp growth in 2022 was close to the high estuaries of the National Bank. Although household demand remained positive in 2022, the growth rate was sluggish. This was caused by high inflation, which negatively affected the real incomes of the population. The growth of consumer lending has also affected demand. At the end of November 2022, consumer loans increased by 24.1% from the beginning of the year to 7.6 trillion tenge. Marketing shares of the largest banks contributed to the growth of consumer lending. In this regard, the dynamics of retail trade shows a steady growth rate. THIRD. FOREIGN ECONOMIC CONDITION. As predicted in the previous decision, the external inflation environment is weakening. Volatility in various commodity markets has been increasing since the beginning of the year. In the oil market, the fixed price of Brent crude oil decreased by 7% to the level of about 80 dollars per barrel. In the short term, the opening of china's borders, which led to an increase in the number of coronavirus cases, caused the oil price to rise. However, China's restrictions could be a drag on global economic growth in the long run. Declining business activity in the industry of many major countries and rising concerns about the risks of recession in the United States and Europe have also contributed to the change in oil prices. The introduction of an embargo in connection with the reduction of oil supplies from Russia and the reduction of oil production in OPEC countries, oil prices were not allowed to fall. World food prices have gradually decreased, but remain high. Since April 2022, the FAO food price index has been declining by 1.9%, which is due to a decline in prices for vegetable oil, cereals and meat. In annual terms, the index fell by 1%. Despite the relaxation of the external inflationary environment, major central banks in developed countries are holding tight monetary policy. The latest decision by the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank was to raise rates by 4.5% and 2.5%. Due to these conditions and weakening pressures, consumer inflation slowed in the world's energy and commodity markets for the first time in a long time. In many countries that are trading partners, inflation is slowing. Inflation in China in December was 1.8%. Consumer inflation in the European Union slowed from a drop in energy prices to 11.1% in November 2022. In Russia, inflation slowed to 12.0%. All these factors will contribute to the reduction of inflation in Kazakhstan. * * * Despite the fact that inflation is based on the projected trajectory, proinflationary risks remain. The main risks of inflation are: - changes in the structure of trade, - accelerated inflation expectations, - preservation of high food inflation, - increase in inflation of regulated goods and services after the period of administrative regulation, - Uncertainty about the war in Ukraine. During the world's potential recession, external demand may be lower than we predicted. The logistics conditions are also creating uncertainty. All of this may contribute to the future level of oil prices, the economic growth trajectory. Taking into account the balance of risks, taking into account that inflation is in line with the base line scenario, the National Bank maintains its position that the base rate rise cycle is nearing its end. Without new shocks, the potential for further base rate increases is limited. Given the proinflationary risks of a high level of inflationary expectations, it is required to keep the base rate in current terms for a long time. Monetary policy easing is possible when inflation and inflation expectations stabilize, this environment in the long term, it will allow us to reach the target route. * * * Dear journalists! The National Bank will continue to adhere to the policy of inflation targeting. We expect inflationary pressure to decrease this year. This will be facilitated by the positive impact of raising the base rate in 2022. Our main task in 2023 is to reduce inflation steadily, return to the target level in the medium term. The next decision on the base rate will be made as a result of the forecast round. During the forecast round, we update our forecasts and estimates. The next decision on the base rate will be announced on February 24, 2023 at 12:00 am Astana time.

Title: Statement of Chairman of the National Bank of Kazakhstan Pirmatov G.O. on the base rate of the National Bank of Kazakhstan, April 7, 2023, Astana
text: Statement of the Chairman of the National Bank of Kazakhstan G.O. Pirmatov on the base rate of the National Bank of Kazakhstan, April 7, 2023, Astana Dear representatives of the mass media! Dear journalists! Good day! Welcome to the National Bank! The Monetary Policy Committee of the National Bank decided to keep the base rate at 16.75%. Annual inflation fell for the first time since the beginning of 2022 and in March it was 18.1%. The decline in inflation is expected and was taken into account in the forecasts of the National Bank. Monthly and base inflation also showed declines, but remained high. The volatility risk of inflation expectations, which fell sharply in February and rose again in March, was partially realized. Thus, some positive changes in the country's inflationary processes have been observed, but it is too early to say that all this change will be a permanent reduction. Despite the positive dynamics, the monthly inflation rate is still much higher than normal. Internal and external factors that will slow down inflation in the future and increase the risk of its acceleration are preserved and partially implemented. The reform of pricing in fuel services will have a direct and indirect impact on inflationary processes. However, in the medium and long term, market prices will positively affect the development of the sectors of the economy and the better forecast of inflationary processes. The increase in public spending and the temporary absence of fiscal principles will also amplify the proinflationary factors. Achieving a sustainable trajectory of inflation remains our main task. In this regard, in accordance with the previously stated position, the National Bank decided to maintain the base rate at the current level in order to support the slowdown in inflationary processes. Our further actions will depend on the updated forecast in May, including the new data and the parameters of reform in the fuel market and housing and communal services. *** I will pay attention to the factors that have caused further decision-making. THE FIRST. INFLATION AND INFLATION EXPECTATIONS DYNAMICS. In March, annual inflation fell to 18.1%. This, along with others, was due to last year's high-base write-offs. There is a slowdown in all components of inflation. At the same time, the increase in prices for fruits and vegetables in the southern regions due to the loss of production, as well as the increase in the cost of transport services due to high demand, has curbed the decline in inflation. Although food inflation slowed significantly in March this year to 20.5%, it continues to contribute a lot to overall inflation. The growth of prices for non-food products slowed to 18.1%, the growth of services - to 14.4%. A slight acceleration in monthly inflation in February had distorted the trend of falling prices. However, monthly inflation slowed to 0.9%. Various estimates of underlying inflation are also slowing down. But they still show a preservation of the highly pro-inflation environment. For example, the annual base inflation, which is excluded from seasonal factors that do not take into account the impact of price increases on fruits and vegetables, regulated services and energy sources, was 19.9%. Nevertheless, it continues to form above the historical average. after the decline, it gained momentum. The median measure of expected inflation was 16.5%. According to the survey, the main factors of inflation are the increase in prices for food and fuel, external conditions, the dynamics of the exchange rate of tenge and the growth of wages and pensions. High and volatile inflation expectations are also one of the main factors holding back the fall in inflation. THE SECOND. THE SITUATION IN THE DOMESTIC ECONOMY. Kazakhstan's economy grew by 4.3% in January-February 2023. This corresponds to the level of 3.5-4.5% set by the National Bank for the current year. The real sector grew by 2.7%, and business activity in the service sector increased by 5.0%. In February of this year, the volume of consumer goods increased in the structure of construction works. Domestic demand is stable. This is evident in the positive dynamics of retail trade turnover. At the end of January-February, retail trade increased by 12.9% in real terms. Despite the low base of the last year, sales of automobiles, electrical equipment, food products and clothing contributed to the growth of trade turnover. External inflationary pressure sits high despite weakening. World food prices are declining. However, it is above the average for the last five years. In this regard, consumer inflation remains high in the United States and the Countries of the European Union. The European Central Bank expects inflation to remain higher for longer. In this regard, the rhetoric of the Federal Reserve System and the European Central Bank remains at an all-time high, despite the problems in the banking sector. Nevertheless, the problems in the United States and European banking sector have affected the dynamics of oil prices. Thus, due to the recession of the world economy and the intensifying risks of reduced demand for crude, oil prices remained slightly below the average level of 88 per barrel in the 2023 base scenario. Despite this, oil prices have begun to recover. And this year, oil prices will be supported by improved demand in China and the OPEC policy. In February 2023, the FAO food price index rose rapidly as a result of lower prices for vegetable oil and dairy products, as well as a slight decline in the cost of grain and meat. Despite the slowdown, large central banks have continued to tighten monetary credit conditions in the face of inflation, which remains high. At the last meeting, the Federal Reserve of the United States raised the rate by 25 basis points to a range of 4.75% -5.0%, and the European Central Bank - by 50 basis points to 3.5%. *** Despite some positive trends in the country's inflation processes, it is too early to say that inflation is steadily declining. The balance of risks remains in a state of proinflationary disposition. This is facilitated by inflationary expectations, which are sensitive to high and short-term price shocks. At the same time, as a result of the increase in prices for regulated goods and services, the risk of accelerating inflation has begun to be realized. The significant revision of state budget expenditures and the temporary suspension of the use of the budgetary principle creates additional proinflationary pressure. Taking into account the above-mentioned risks, the dynamics of inflation and its compliance with forecasts, the Monetary Policy Committee will take a previously stated position on the need for a first hold. This will allow to support a significant slowdown in inflationary processes initiated, reduce inflationary pressure from rising budget expenditures and prevent inflationary expectations from stabilizing at a high level. Further decisions on the base rate will depend on the output of new data, including the parameters of the reform, which we will consider when upgrading the forecast in May 2023. We do not plan to take action on the direct impact on inflation from rising fuel prices. At the same time, when making decisions on monetary policy, we will carefully monitor and analyze the additional effects, including changes in prices for related commodities, inflation expectations. Taking into account the stated inflation risks, the National Bank will continue to maintain the current monetary conditions. *** Dear journalists! The main task of the National Bank is to ensure price stability, for which we will continue to pursue a disinflationary monetary policy, which will facilitate the further easing of inflation and the achievement of targeted guidelines in the medium term. The next decision on the base rate will be determined in accordance with the results of the next forecast round and will be announced on May 26, 2023 at 12:00 p.m. Astana time.

Title: Statement of the Chairman of the National Bank of Kazakhstan Pirmatov G.O. on the base rate of the National Bank of Kazakhstan May 26, 2023, Astana
text: Statement of the Chairman of the National Bank of Kazakhstan Pirmatov G.O. on the base rate of the National Bank of Kazakhstan May 26, 2023, Astana Dear representatives of the mass media! Dear journalists! Good day! Welcome to the National Bank! The Monetary Policy Committee of the National Bank decided to keep the base rate at 16.75%. Today's decision was made on the basis of an analysis of forecasts, taking into account specific data and new factors. In addition to upgrading forecasts of macroeconomic indicators, we have also brought inflation risk assessment to a new balance. Our assessment shows a slight disinflationary disinflationof the balance of risks. The external sector's pressure on prices weakened slightly. The reason for this is the decline in the growth rate of world food prices and a significant slowdown in inflation in the trading partner countries of Kazakhstan. Due to the stable exchange rate, the slowest growth of external prices creates favorable conditions for the reduction of inflation in the country. However, the fiscal stimulus continues, sustained domestic demand, high inflation expectations and fuel prices for heating and housing and communal services the proinflationary impact of internal factors is maintained due to the rise. The decision will contribute to the further suspension of inflationary processes in the country in order to stabilize and reduce price growth in the medium term. *** Let's focus on the main factors of the decision. THE FIRST. REAL AND EXPECTED INFLATION DYNAMICS In April 2023, annual inflation in line with our expectations continued the process of decline, which began in March and amounted to 16.8%. Food inflation slowed to 17.9% due to the stabilization of supply in the fruit and vegetable market. Prices for non-food products increased by 18.2%, and fuel prices increased. The cost of services increased by 13.7%, which is due to the stable demand for individual services. It should be noted that the increase in prices for goods and services has not yet reflected the indirect effects of rising fuel prices. The monthly inflation rate in March and April of this year was 0.9%, above the average historical values. However, as a result of monetary policy, the basic Various inflation estimates show a gradual slowdown in the stable components of inflation. However, the indirect effects of the increase in prices for fuel and utilities contribute to its dynamics. In general, despite the slowdown, inflationary processes maintain an inertia nature, keeping domestic demand stable. As a result of the changed geopolitical situation, the process of rebuilding the logistics and production supply routes is affecting the price growth. The results of the survey of enterprises of the real sector also confirm the increase in prices. Stimulating fiscal policy and high inflationary expectations remain important proinflationary factors. In April this year, the expected inflation for the next 12 months increased to 16.7%. The planned increase in tariffs for housing and utilities services and the actual increase in fuel prices have partially affected public expectations. Despite the fact that the inflation rate has decreased significantly, it is still showing a high value. That is, it is too early to say about the positive trend seen in the dynamics of expected and felt inflation. THE SECOND. FACTORS OF THE DOMESTIC ECONOMY In January-April of this year, the real GDP of Kazakhstan grew by 5.0%, which is higher than our forecast estimate. The production of goods and services is also growing. Construction, trade, information and communications showed the highest growth rates. The dynamics of the business activity index, which has been positive in recent months, confirms positive trends in the real sector of the daconomics. The demand of the population remains stable. This is evident in data on retail trade turnover, import of consumer goods and non-cash payments of the population for goods and services. It should be noted that the growth rate of retail sales has reached pre-pandemic values. High levels of consumer lending and inflation expectations will support the expansion of non-food trade. Nominal wages and incomes of the population are growing. According to the survey, 30% of respondents noted that the level of income exceeds 300 thousand tenge. A year ago, the share of such responses was in the range of 10-15%. Nevertheless, real incomes of the population are falling against the background of high inflation, hindering the active implementation of consumer demand. Support for the economy with government programs high investment activity is one of the drivers of domestic demand. In January-April of this year, investments in fixed assets increased by 18% in real terms. In particular, the volume of investments in transport and storage increased by 39.3%, agriculture - by 26.5%, industry - by 18.1%, real estate transactions - by 10.0%. THIRD. EXTERNAL ECONOMIC CONDITION Global inflation is expected to fall further. It is facilitated by the reduction of pressure on raw materials and commodity markets and the solution of logistics issues. Despite a significant increase in April this year, the FAO's food price index maintained its trend of decline. As part of the large-scale production and grain transactions, the price of grain crops will be increased faster than previously forecasted. In this regard, due to the stable exchange rate of tenge, there is a possibility of further slowdown in the growth of domestic food prices. The additional disinflation factor is the low rate of inflation in the trading partner countries of Kazakhstan. This is especially the result of last year's high base in Russia and the low demand for goods due to the uneven economic recovery in China. Gradual improvement in inflation however, external monetary conditions in many countries remain constraining. Annual price growth figures have exceeded the target rate. The oil market will develop more smoothly than previously estimated. The assumption that China's economy will recover quickly after the removal of the Covid restrictions has not been fulfilled. At the same time, maintaining a fairly tight monetary policy in the framework of stable inflation increases the risk of a global recession. Oil production cuts on the part of OPEC have failed to have a positive impact on price restraint. Thus, the impact of inhibitor factors on the decline in the cost of prevailing oil has led to a revision of the forecast estimate. To form our forecasts, we also revised the trajectory of brent crude oil prices on the basis of these factors. According to the basic scenario, the average price of oil in 2023 will be 82.2 dollars per barrel. *** Note the updated forecasts of macroeconomic indicators. Taking into account the existing external and internal factors, as well as new prerequisites, inflation forecasts were revised upwards. Our Updated according to our forecasts, annual inflation in 2023 11-14% will be formed within 9-11% in 2024 and 5.5-7.5% in 2025. The change in the forecast estimate for price growth is primarily due to the impact of the direct and indirect effects of the increase in the cost of fuel and housing services. Price increases will lead to a slow decline in inflation to the medium term target. This year, the fiscal momentum is viewed as pro-cyclical. Based on the parameters set out in the forecast of socio-economic development, it is expected that in 20242025 years it will weaken as part of the planned return to compliance with the countercyclical budgetary rule. Let me note that this is an important prerequisite for our forecast. The restraining nature of monetary conditions, improved foreign economic conditions, will have a restraining effect on inflation. It is associated with a further decline in food prices and low inflation in trade partner countries. The risks of inflation outlook include stronger fiscal stimulus, stronger indirect effects from rising prices for fuel and housing services, longer-term effects on pricing of logistics and industrial supply routes, and the possibility of inflation expectations remaining at high levels. Qazaqstan ekonomkasy osyini 2023 jyla boljamy improved. Gdp growth in 2023 will be in the range of 4.2-5.2%. The economic growth forecast for 20242025 remained unchanged at 3.5-4.5%. Prices for the current year were revised taking into account the actual dynamics of gdp. This will be influenced by stimulating fiscal policy, stable domestic demand and expectations of higher external demand. At the same time, the positive dynamics of imports, the real interest rate, formed along with the stronger real exchange rate of tenge, will balance economic activity, reducing the pressure on inflation. The risks of gdp projections are due to concerns about the sustainability of global inflation. This would lead central banks to keep up with the tough rhetoric. It, in turn, affects oil demand and increases the risk of recession in developed countries. Another negative factor of the economy's growth forecast is the problems that may arise in the way kazakhstan exports to international markets. According to our estimates, taking into account the positive dynamics of real inflation, monetary conditions have reached a restraining point. In this regard, the National Bank in the second half of this year normal and serious lying down it is. The decisions we make will depend on the compliance of price increases with the estimated estimates, the persistent slowdown in base inflation from the indirect effects of rising prices for fuel and housing services, the dynamics of inflation expectations, as well as the preservation of budgetary principles in the formation of the budget for 2024-2025. At the same time, the probability of lowering the base rate in the next decision is not high. *** Dear journalists! The National Bank will continue to conduct monetary policy to ensure the stability of prices. For more information on the adopted decision-takers, inflation forecasts and risks, please see the report on monetary policy, which will be published on June 5. The next decision on the base rate will be announced on July 5, 2023 at 12:00 am Astana time.

Title: Statement of Chairman of the National Bank of Kazakhstan Pirmatov G.O. on the base rate of the National Bank of Kazakhstan, July 5, 2023, Astana
text: Statement of Chairman of the National Bank of Kazakhstan G.O. Pirmatov on the base rate of the National Bank of Kazakhstan July 5, 2023, Astana Dear representatives of the mass media! Dear journalists, good day! Welcome to the National Bank! The Monetary Policy Committee of the National Bank decided to keep the base rate at 16.75%. Prices growth has slowed considerably. The annual and monthly inflation figures are falling. However, in the stable part of inflation, the rate of slowdown is still weak. Inflation expectations are showing an increase due to news of higher prices for fuel and housing services. Lower food costs, slower price growth in trade partner countries and rising interest rates from central banks have put external pressure on inflation. But domestic factors are still hampering the sustained low price growth. Domestic factors include, along with inflationary expectations, stable domestic demand and fiscal momentum. With that in mind, we will continue to take a serious approach to decision-making in line with previous rhetoric. To date, our main task is to ensure a steady decline in inflation. *** I want to pay attention to the factors that have caused the further decision. THE FIRST. INFLATION AND INFLATION EXPECTATIONS DYNAMICS. Annual inflation in the forecast range was 14.6% in June. Food and non-food components contribute a lot to the overall decline in inflation. The growth of food prices slowed significantly in June and amounted to 14.6%. Inflation of non-food products decreased to 15.8%. The increase in the cost of services corresponds to the projected trajectory and amounted to 13.3% in June. Monthly inflation slowed to 0.5%. A number of assessments of base inflation were carried out. In this regard, in recent months, we have seen that the stable components of price growth in the economy have slowed slightly. This is due to the preservation of the pro-inflation environment. High inflation expectations are one of the factors holding back the fall in inflation. Nevertheless, the preservation of its high and unstable dynamics is due to the increase in prices for fuel and housing services. We have taken it into account in advance when making decisions at the base rate. The median of inflation, expected for the next year, rose to 17.2% in June. The inflation rate has fallen to 18.8%, but remains high. THE SECOND. TRENDS IN THE DOMESTIC ECONOMY. Kazakhstan's economy grew by 4.5% in January-May 2023. This is in line with the forecasts set by the National Bank for the current year. The real sector grew by 3.6%, business activity in the services sector increased by 4.9%. The highest growth rates were observed in construction, trade, information and communications. Positive trends in economic growth are confirmed by the dynamics of the business activity index. It increased to 51.1 in June. Consumer credit and high inflation expectations are contributing to the sustainability of domestic demand. It can be seen in the dynamics of the trade turnover and the growth of imports of consumer goods. The expansion of investment activity has also positively affected domestic demand. In January-May this year, the growth of investments in fixed assets amounted to 17.2% in real terms. The main volume of investments was accounted for the construction and overhaul. The decline in real incomes due to inflation, which is still high, is a constraint on consumer demand. THIRD. FOREIGN ECONOMIC CONDITION. The external sector is dominated by factors contributing to the slowdown in price growth. In the world, there is a further decline in food prices, low inflation in the trading partner countries of Kazakhstan and the readiness of central banks in developed countries to increase rates further. In May this year, world food prices decreased by 2.6%. The cost of vegetable oils, cereals and dairy products is decreasing. Within the framework of the more favorable conditions for harvesting in the upcoming season, the real dynamics of grain prices was lower than we expected. Accordingly, domestic food prices have the potential to slow further in terms of growth. Consumer inflation in Russia and China remains at low levels. The Bank of Russia has signaled that the period of rising inflation has begun in May and that it is possible to raise the key rate. As a result of monetary policy in the European Union, price growth is gradually slowing. And inflation remains stable. This will lead to tougher rhetoric from the European Central Bank. A similar trend is observed in the United States. There, the Federal Reserve System announced that the rate could rise further. Thus, a hand to the designated target routes within the framework of expectations due to the long delivery period external monetary requirements are constantly increasing. The situation in the oil market is uncertain, primarily due to future demand. Higher interest rates are increasing the risks of a possible recession. According to forecasts, china's economy, which will account for half of this year's oil demand growth, is recovering weakly. The OPEC announcement of additional oil production cuts and forecasts of a near-term oil shortage were not enough to support prices. As a result, the cost of oil is currently lower than the base scenario. *** It is too early to say about the credible sustainable trend of inflation decline, without the expectations and expectations seen in the country's inflationary processes. This is due to domestic inflation factors and possible risks to future price growth. The main risks include high inflation expectations, the realization of indirect effects from higher prices for fuel and housing services, increased fiscal stimulus, the possibility of a global recession affecting oil demand, and growing geopolitical uncertainty. We will act in accordance with the earlier rhetoric. The above-mentioned factors and risks require the observed implementation of monetary policy. The current level of the base rate will support the process of slowing down stable inflation, balance the growth of public spending and prevent inflationary expectations from stabilizing at a high level. We see that the observed decline in inflation has begun to allow the base rate to fall. The next decision will be made alongwith updating forecasts and analyzing new data. In this regard, we will consider the possibility of reducing the base rate in August. All our efforts are aimed at achieving the target of 5% inflation in the medium term. *** Dear journalists! In the course of today's statement, please adjust our inflation target. Last year, in the Strategic Plan of the National Bank, we outlined an analysis of the medium-term objectives of monetary policy in inflation. We are not only investing our efforts in this work, but also from our country and abroad, fundamental and fundamental work involving researchers we're done. The results of the research were presented at the scientific and practical conference held in April. A comprehensive analysis using different approaches and an overview of international practice showed the following: The point-of-point format of the target is considered acceptable in terms of communication and stabilization of inflation expectations; The optimal inflation target for our economy is not higher than 4% and not more than 7%. Many estimates show the optimality of the inflation target of 5%. In this regard, the National Bank made the following decision: First, to clarify the previously announced inflation target, replacing interval values with a point format from 2023. This will provide clarity and clarity on the central bank's policy objectives and clearly demonstrate the commitment of monetary policy to a clear goal. Secondly, in the medium term, the inflation target is to maintain annual inflation at the level of 5%. The selected target ensures consistency and continuity in the formation of the target and contributes to inflation and expectations of about 5%. Achieving the target will increase the effectiveness of the policy and create a more stable environment for investment and economic growth in the long term. The next decision on the base rate will be announced on August 25, 2023 at 12:00 am Astana time.

Title: Statement of Chairman of the National Bank of Kazakhstan Suleimenov T.M. on the base rate of the National Bank of Kazakhstan dated October 6, 2023 Astana
text: The National Bank of The Republic of Kazakhstan about the base rate Suleimenov T.M. Statement 2023 jyly 6 qazan, Astana Dear journalists! Good day! Welcome to the National Bank! The Monetary Policy Committee of the National Bank decided to reduce the base rate to 16% or 0.5%. The decision was made taking into account the positive dynamics of inflationary processes. Annual inflation is actively slowing. Inflation indicators, which do not take into account the underlying inflation and seasonal factors, are stabilizing. Inflation expectations remain volatile and are at a high level. External inflation slowed and positively. This is facilitated by the reduction of world food prices and the policy of central banks to ensure price stability. However, it is important to pay attention to some of the risks. In particular: the stability of basic inflation in the world, inflation rates by a number of trade and partner countries increased pressure, the impact of oil prices on global inflation, and the strengthening of geopolitical risks. In our economy, fiscal stimulus and sustained domestic demand have put pressure on prices. This, together with high inflation expectations, will allow to create an indirect effect from the increase in prices for housing and utilities services and fuel and lubricants( fuel and lubricants). Previously, it was suspended to some extent by the positive dynamics of tenge exchange rate. The risks of rising prices were added to the likelihood of a significant increase in the cost of food this year due to the deterioration of wheat crop forecasts. In this case, we will make a decision that corresponds to the rhetoric of the Previously Voiced National Bank. The National Bank is striving to implement a disinflationary policy. In turn, it requires the preservation of the base rate in real terms. That is, the current rate of inflation is higher than the rate of economic growth. As you know, the gradual slowdown in inflation near the lower end of the 10-12% forecast corridor contributed to the realization of the possibility of a reduction of the base rate in the course of this decision. At the same time, due to the above mentioned risks, the possibility of further rate reduction until the end of 2023 is quite limited. Our main task is to ensure a stable decline in inflation and stabilize it to the medium-term target of about 5%. Now I will pay attention to the factors of the decision. THE FIRST. DYNAMICS OF INFLATION AND INFLATION EXPECTATIONS. In September this year, annual inflation slowed to 11.8%. Inflation continues to fall due to tight monetary policy and the gradual exit of last year's high base. At the same time, a significant factor is the incomplete implementation of the Government's plan regarding tariff reforms. Thus, the data on the proportion of increase in tariffs for regulated services show that only half of the reforms for 9 months have been implemented. The reform will be continued. In general, inflation remains at the lower end of the forecast range - 10-12%. At the same time, there was a decrease in food inflation and an increase in the share of paid services. Food inflation slowed to 11.4%. Inflation of non-food products decreased to 12.1%. Increase in prices for services The most normal increase in tariffs for housing and communal services within the framework of the pace was 11.9%. Since tariffs are not raised evenly, not all regions are covered. Monthly inflation in September was 0.6%, and continued to be significantly higher than both historical and our target. The median of the base inflation, that is, its constant part, is calculated on the basis of monthly data that do not take into account seasonal factors. Over the past six months, its value has remained unchanged at 0.7%. Despite the stabilization, it remains at a higher level than the target. In this case, we believe it is too early to talk about the sustainability of the trend of inflation reduction. Due to fiscal stimulus and high inflation expectations on the basis of a further slowdown in inflation, it is constrained by sustained domestic demand. As for inflationary expectations, they have increased further, adapted to changes in the situation in certain commodities markets and have formed at a high level. In September, the median inflation estimate for the next year was 17.0%. The inflation rate was 17.8%. The growth of housing and utilities services and fuel prices is a cause for concern among respondents. THE SECOND. TRENDS IN THE DOMESTIC ECONOMY. Kazakhstan's economy grew by 4.9% in January-August this year. This corresponds to the forecasts of the National Bank. Due to steady domestic demand, implementation of infrastructure projects and the recovery of the oil sector, the scope of business activity has expanded. The growth in commodity production amounted to 4.4%, business activity in the services sector increased by 4.8%. Construction, trade, information and communications showed the highest growth rates, including the construction of infrastructure buildings. At the same time, the index of business activity in September amounted to 49.0, due to the prolongation of the delivery period, the increase in the cost of utilities and logistics costs of production. The data on rising producer prices in the industrial sector is of particular concern. This could highly reflect the risk of the indirect impact of the housing and utilities reforms. In January-August 2023, retail trade increased by 7.3% in annual terms. This indicates the stability of domestic demand, along with the growth of the population's credit, import of consumer goods. At the same time, the expansion of investment activity to support domestic demand, the growth of real incomes of the population and budget expenditures on transfers affects. In January-August, the increase in investments in fixed assets amounted to 12.2% per annum. Construction and construction and overhaul of the building constitute the main volume of investments. In the medium term, the factor of proinflation is the decline in wheat production expected this year, which will lead to an increase in food prices. In the meanwhile, we believe that the relevant departments should keep this issue under control. THIRD. FOREIGN ECONOMIC CONDITION. In the external sector, despite the general expected slowdown in global inflation, there are certain proinflationfactors and a stronger risk role. The world's core inflation indicators are still stable and are being formed in higher values than the established target slots. Therefore, the stability of inflationary processes will push up the timing of rate cuts in developed countries and lead to a tightening of the central banks' policy. In the background of tighter monetary policy, rising oil prices, high inflation and continued economic uncertainty, there has been a decline in global business activity. At the same time, real inflation dynamics is observed in a number of key trade-partner countries with Kazakhstan, in particular, in the EU and Russia. Prices in the European Union slowed to a slower pace than expected, suggesting a rapid increase in prices for services and food. Thus, the forecasts for inflation for 2023 and 2024 were revised upwards. After the recent increase in core interest rates, it is expected to remain at its current level for a long time. Inflation in Russia has been on the rise for much longer, creating conditions for tighter monetary conditions, as domestic demand increases and the rouble weakens. China has seen signs of improvement in economic activity. They are evident in a slight acceleration in inflation and an improvement in business and consumer activity. Monetary conditions in China remain at an encouraging footing. In the UNITED States, the trend of falling inflation is felt to be slow. Even at the end of August, inflation rose above market expectations. The main factor is the increase in oil prices. In these circumstances, the Federal Reserve has expressed its intention to keep the rate on hold for a long time, rather than rule out the possibility of a rate increase this year. Food prices in the world decreased by 2.1% in August. The decrease was due to the decline in prices for dairy products, vegetable oil, meat and cereals during the normal increase in sugar prices. The oil market is characterized by positive dynamics. This is due to the decline in u.S. crude oil inventories and opec actions to cut oil production by the end of the year as demand for energy in China gradually begins to recover. As a result, the oil price is currently close to the level of the optimistic scenario. * * * In conclusion, it should be noted that despite some positive trends in inflationary processes, prices for a wide range of goods and services in the country continue to rise. In such cases, we must maintain a consistent approach and act in accordance with previously stated rhetoric. As previously noted, annual inflation is gradually slowing to 10-12% on a trajectory that is near the low end of forecasts. This has contributed to the implementation of the possibility of a reduction of the base rate today. But due to the existence of a number of proinflationary risks both in the external sector and within the economy, it significantly limits the ability to reduce it until the end of this year. Therefore, until the end of the year, monetary policy easing will be considered in the event that annual inflation slows to a single-value level of at least 10%. Tight monetary conditions will help to reduce inflation to the lower end of the forecast corridor of 10-12% by the end of 2023, as well as stabilize the medium-term horizon close to the target of 5%. The National Bank monitors the target ingenuity trajectory of annual inflation in order to react to possible fluctuations in a timely fashion. * * * Dear journalists! The National Bank will continue to implement the disinflationary monetary policy. We rely on the principles of the inflation targeting regime. At the same time, we will work closely and actively with the Government to strengthen monetary and fiscal policy coordination. I am confident that our joint actions will contribute to the creation of macroeconomic conditions for the growth of the welfare of citizens of Kazakhstan. We can confidently say that we can achieve medium-term targets of 5%. The main task of the National Bank is to ensure price stability. We will make every effort to achieve the target of 5% inflation in the medium term. The next decision on the base rate will be based on the results of the forecast round. The next decision on the level of the base rate will be announced on November 24 at 12:00 am Astana time. Now we are ready to answer your questions.

Title: Statement of the Chairman of the National Bank of Kazakhstan Suleimenov T.M. on the base rate of the National Bank, November 24, 2023, Astana
text: Statement of the Chairman of the National Bank of Kazakhstan Suleimenov T.M. on the base rate of the National Bank of Kazakhstan dated November 24, 2023, Astana Dear representatives of the mass media! Dear journalists! Good day! Welcome to the National Bank! The Monetary Policy Committee of the National Bank decided to reduce the base rate by 25 basis points to 15.75%. Our decision will take into account the updated forecasts of inflation and economic growth, as well as the results of the analysis of real data and the balance of risks. We see the slowdown in inflation due to previous decisions on the rate, measures taken by the Government and akims, as well as the base. Recall that inflation was very high last year and its effects have contributed to a moderate slowdown in annual inflation this year. Currently, it is at the low end of the previous forecast. In turn, inflation indicators that do not take into account the underlying inflation and seasonal factors are stabilizing. In the coming months, the annual inflation rate is expected to reach single digits. factors and risks are increasing. In particular, the growth of food prices, inflation in the Russian Federation as our main trading partner, the dynamics of inflation expectations and fiscal expenditures. Nevertheless, the slowing rate of annual inflation and the relatively low outlook until the end of 2023 have helped to lower the base rate in this time of decision. Further, the trends in inflation expectations, budget policy parameters and the external environment that we control require us to maintain tight monetary conditions for a long time. Now I want to focus on the factors that have caused the decision. THE FIRST. DYNAMICS OF INFLATION AND INFLATION EXPECTATIONS. Inflation is slowing from eight months. In October this year, annual inflation was at the level of 10.8%. Real inflation will be near the lower end of the forecast range for the current year. This is primarily due to the normal increase in prices for housing and utilities and non-food products. Annual growth in prices for goods slowed to 10.4%.
