Annual inflation of non-food products decreased to 11.1%. The increase in prices for services decreased to 11.0%. Monthly inflation in October was 0.7%, in line with the historical average. At the same time, in the context of the decline in annual inflation, we see stabilization of the base inflation (0.6% for the second month in a row) and a slowdown in inflation, which does not take into account seasonal factors. This reflects the trend towards stabilization of inflationary processes. However, the dynamics of the stable part of inflation are still above target. Inflation expectations are rising regardless of the positive trend of real inflation and may change depending on the situation in some commodities markets. The main factors are the increase in fuel prices and the dynamics of food prices. THE SECOND. TRENDS IN THE DOMESTIC ECONOMY. Kazakhstan in January-October 2023 the gdp grew by 4.9%. Sustainable domestic demand, implementation of infrastructure projects and oil business activity due to the recovery of the sector expanding. Business activity increased by 5.4% per year. Construction (12.5%), trade (10.4% of GDP), information and communications (8.0%) show the highest growth rates. The volume of production in the agricultural sector decreased by 8.6% per year. This could pose a certain risk to food inflation in the future. Dynamic growth of industries in the economy, based on recovery of oil production and public expenditures, continues. This, in turn, illustrates the risk of "overheating" and is a proinflationary factor. Consumer demand of the population can also be attributed to proinflationary factors. Its stable dynamics is confirmed by data on consumer lending and imports of consumer goods. For 9 months of 2023, imports of non-food consumer goods increased by 36.7%. Such growth rates indicate that domestic demand exceeds domestic supply opportunities. At the same time, the expansion of investment activity by 12.6% and the increase in real wages of the population by 3.5% support domestic demand. THIRD. FOREIGN ECONOMIC CONDITION. There is a decrease in inflationary pressure in the external sector. This means that the monetary policy has slowed down for a period of time. Nevertheless, we expect the impact of proinflationary factors to be significantly stronger in the short term. This is due to the inflation dynamics in Russia and the expected rise in world food prices. Further, when the situation in the trading partner countries stabilizes, we expect the achievement of target values and external factors to ease the proinflationary pressure. As our main trading partner, inflation in Russia is accelerating. It was 6.7% in October compared to 6.0% in September. Thus, it was higher than previous forecasts. The reason for this is the growing domestic demand and the weakening of the ruble. At the same time, as part of the Bank of Russia's consistent tightening of monetary policy, we expect inflation in Russia to return to the forecast corridor in 2025. In the European Union, price growth slowed to 3.6% from 4.9% in September from the previous year's high base. According to updated forecasts, inflation in the European Union in 2024 will be much higher than expected, but the policy of keeping the higher rate for longer will allow the EU to reach its target in 2025. China experienced deflation in October due to the current weak economic activity data. As part of the reduction in prices for all types of food, with the exception of sugar, world food prices are falling. The decline in grain prices was due to a seasonal increase in supply. However, prices may start to rise in late 2023 and early 2024 as the supply of grain from Ukraine decreases. The oil market is stabilizing at about 80 dollars per barrel. As for the proposal, opec decision to cut oil production by the end of the year and the risk of further escalation of tensions in the Middle East put upward pressure on oil prices. Taking this into account, in our base scenario, the price of Brent crude oil is projected at an average of 85 dollars in 2024 and 80 dollars in 2025. *** This year, inflation in the baseline scenario is projected at 9.3-10.3%. The revision of the forecast for this year is due to a moderate increase in tariffs for housing and communal services and prices for non-food products. In the medium term, the weakening of external environment pressure and the tightmonetary nature of monetary policy will help to reduce inflation. the forecast was maintained at 5.5-7.5%. During these periods, the main risks of the inflation forecast are the strengthening of fiscal stimulus, the lack of stabilization of inflationary expectations, the possibility of an increase in food prices due to low yields of grain in 2023, and the increase in tariffs for housing utilities. At the same time, the inflation forecast does not take into account the increase in value added tax (VAT) in 2025, discussed by the Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan. We can assess its impact on inflation when the parameters of these tax reforms are clear. Because the potential increase in VAT is a one-time factor and does not require a monetary policy response, we will carefully monitor the secondary effects and act accordingly if they occur. This year, kazakhstan's GDP growth forecasts remained unchanged in the range of 4.2-5.2%, and they were revised in the medium term. The forecast for 2024 was revised down to a range of 3.2-4.2%. This is due to the start of increasing production at Tengizchevroil by the end of 2024 or by 2025. Accordingly, the forecast for 2025 was increased by 5.5-6.5% against the background of the inability to produce the previously planned volume of oil and the slower gdp growth in 2024. The rapid decline in annual inflation and its low expectations until the end of 2023 have helped to lower the base rate. The decisions taken at the base rate depend on the compliance of the inflation dynamics with the projected trajectory. If inflation slows further in 2024, the National Bank will reconsider a moderate rate cut while maintaining tight monetary conditions in the medium term to stabilize inflation expectations. The goal is to return inflation to the target of 5% and to meet inflation expectations. In this case, there may also be a delay in changing the base rate to gather data and monitor the balance of risks. *** Dear journalists! The main task of the National Bank is to ensure price stability. We will make every effort to achieve the target of 5% inflation in the medium term. Detailed information on the factors, inflation forecasts and risks that have caused the decision can be found in the Monetary Policy Report, which will be published on December 4, 2023.

Title: Report of The Deputy Chairman of the National Bank of The Republic of Kazakhstan V. Tutushkin "On socio-economic development and results of execution of the republican budget for January-November 2023" at a meeting of the Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan
text: Report of The Deputy Chairman of the National Bank of The Republic of Kazakhstan V. Tutushkin "On socio-economic development and results of execution of the republican budget for January-November 2023" at a meeting of the Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan Dear Alikhan Askhanuly! The price of paid services - tariffs for housing and utilities services, internet and airline tickets - has increased. In the coming months, annual inflation is expected to reach a one-point rate, or below 10%. The reduction in annual inflation and its forecasts allowed to lower the base rate to 15.75%. On the other hand, there is an increase in seasonal demand from importers. To him the revival of the cycle of implementation of projects will have the most impact Sit down. National Bank to adhere to free floating exchange rate regime and currency interventions do not do this. Slide 5. INTERNATIONAL RESERVES Total international reserves in November Soynda 92.7 bln. Gold and foreign exchange reserves of the National Bank decreased by 2.8% (to 34.1 billion DOLLARS) since the beginning of the year. This is due to the reduction of the second-tier banks' funds in the foreign exchange accounts of the Republic of Kazakhstan and the conversion of currency by the Ministry of Finance to pay its obligations. The assets of the National Fund increased by 5.2% (to 58.6 billion US dollars) since the beginning of the year. This was due to the growth of investment income by 7.9% (or 4.4 billion DOLLARS) since the beginning of the year. Total revenues to the fund amounted to 4.4 trillion tenge since the beginning of the year. Transfers from the National Fund to the republican budget amounted to 3.9 trillion tenge, including the amount of the purchase of shares of JSC "NC "KazMunayGas" to finance the republican budget. 74 billion tenge was allocated from the beginning of the year for the purchase of bonds of JSC "NWF "SamrukKazyna" to finance the project "Dostyk-Moyinty". SLIDE 6. BIRYAI JINAQTAySHY ZEYNETAQY QORYNY ZEYNETAQY ASSETS Single accumulative pension fund pension assets show positive dynamics. They increased by 18.6% from the beginning of the year to 17.3 trillion tenge. The volume of investment income amounted to 1.3 trillion tenge since the beginning of the year. Pension contributions amounted to 1.9 trillion tenge, and the amount of early withdrawal amounted to about 255 billion tenge. * * * Dear Alikhan Askhanuly! The National Bank will monitor the development of the situation in foreign and domestic markets, and will continue to work on ensuring macroeconomic stability and reducing inflation further. Thank you for your attention!
